rises in white towers and old stone, a city of lecture halls, wards, and polished cruelty. Pela Dianthus knows every shortcut between dormitory and classroom. She knows which stairs echo, which windows reflect her pink skin too clearly, and which corridors fill with students who whisper the word demon like it is a diagnosis. Today Professor Ardenfelt is teaching elemental affinity. Pela has waited months for this lesson.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Remember where Pela came from->Memory of Brittanica Ultima]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">The corridor is crowded enough that Pela has to turn sideways to pass. Students in pressed uniforms laugh around her as if the sound itself has been trained to avoid her. Her books are heavy. Her parents' last letter is folded between the pages of Advanced Elemental Forms, where she can feel it but not see it. How does Pela cross the hall?</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">(link: "Hold the books tight and keep her head down.")[(set: $shame to $shame + 1)(set: $nerve to $nerve - 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Shame")(goto: "Books To Chest")]</div><div class="choice-row">(link: "Meet the stares for once.")[(set: $nerve to $nerve + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Nerve")(goto: "Meet The Stares")]</div><div class="choice-row">(link: "Count the warding runes along the ceiling.")[(set: $research to $research + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Research")(goto: "Count The Runes")]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela folds herself small around her books. There is a technique to vanishing while still taking up space: no sudden movements, no eye contact, no sound that could become a reason. It does not work.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Someone crashes into her->The Collision]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela looks up. One student glances away first. Another smirks because looking away would admit she had been caught. Pela's ears flatten, but she does not lower her eyes. Her books scatter. Her knees hit stone. "Keep crying, weak little half-demon," the student says, already walking away. "Maybe go back to whatever dark cave you came from." No one helps. Someone laughs into their sleeve. Pela gathers her notes page by page, the ink blurring where her hand shakes.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">(link: "Swallow the words and hurry on.")[(set: $shame to $shame + 1)(set: $nerve to $nerve - 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Shame")(goto: "Outside Ardenfelt")]</div><div class="choice-row">(link: "Whisper that she belongs here.")[(set: $nerve to $nerve + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Nerve")(goto: "Outside Ardenfelt")]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Professor Ardenfelt's classroom waits at the end of the hall. It means every direction can become a mistake.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Listen to Odelyn's fear->Ch7 A New Path 30]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Before the stranger reaches her, Pela notices the green and the cut of his uniform. Royal. Angry. Moving like someone who expects hallways to clear for him.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Answer him carefully->Ch7 A New Path 09]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">The shadow in the corner thickens like smoke remembering it used to be a person. Pela looks up too late. The book has not been speaking alone.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Notice what else entered->Ch7 A New Path 21]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela moves because hesitation will hurt more than ignorance. Her parry is ugly, loud, and barely in time. Odelyn accepts it only as a beginning.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Meet Odelyn's charge->Ch7 A New Path 36]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I will be careful," Pela says. Lysander studies her like he knows careful is a promise people make before they understand the price of keeping it. "Good. Start by surviving your own temper."</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear what he is->Ch7 A New Path 17]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I will try," Pela says. Odelyn closes her eyes as if she wants to believe the words and knows better than to rest anything precious on them.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear what promises are worth->Ch7 A New Path 31]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"You do not get to call me stupid because you are scared," Pela says. Odelyn's hand tightens in Pela's tie. "I get to call you alive while you still are."</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Meet Odelyn's grip->Ch7 A New Path 24]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela listens past the polite words. Protect means contain. Essential means watched. Safety means the academy has decided she is both student and risk. The darkness around the room makes the translation easy.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Agree with clearer eyes->Ch7 A New Path 07]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Odelyn's spear has rhythm: feint, pressure, punish, retreat. Pela catches the pattern just before the first strike lands. Understanding it does not make blocking easy. It makes blocking possible.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Meet Odelyn's charge->Ch7 A New Path 36]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Elijah wants her cornered. Pela sees it in the shape of his voice: accusation, title, death, no space to answer. Knowing the tactic does not make it harmless. It only tells her where the knife is meant to enter.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear the threat again->Ch7 A New Path 12]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Outside the office, Pela replays the Dean's warning word by word. No sentence openly threatened her. That is what makes it feel practiced. Powerful people rarely need to raise their voices when the building already belongs to them.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Keep walking->Ch7 A New Path 08]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela fights the sleep for one breath. The room tilts. Odelyn's shadowed hand is cold against her forehead. Pela keeps her eyes open long enough to see that Odelyn is crying.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Fall into The Lost->Ch7 A New Path 26]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I am fine," Pela lies. Odelyn gives her a look that says she has seen better lies from worse liars. She does not challenge it. Not here, not with the hallway still humming from Pela's voice.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Lysander speak->Ch7 A New Path 15]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela catches the thought as it forms: I need power or they will kill me. Then she hears the book inside the need, polishing fear until it looks like destiny. The realization hurts, but it gives her something to hold that is not the grimoire.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Listen for the spark->Ch7 A New Path 45]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela thinks of Gareth at her door, Odelyn crying in the dark, the strange mercy in people who keep warning her instead of leaving. The blade steadies around that feeling. Not rage. Not destiny. A reason to come back whole.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Move with control->Ch7 A New Path 46]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela tries to defend herself with words, but fear gets there first. The academy hallway narrows. Elijah's face becomes every threat wearing one expression, and Pela answers like someone with nowhere left to retreat.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the outburst break loose->Ch7 A New Path 12]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela stands outside the Dean's door until the silence becomes accusing. Every possible punishment rehearses itself in her head. Only when she realizes she is shaking does she knock.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Enter the Dean's office->Ch7 A New Path 02]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela steps back because promises need room to become action. Odelyn watches her face, searching for the book, the anger, the girl underneath both. Pela lets herself be seen.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let go gently->Ch7 A New Path 48]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela takes the seat because refusing would make her look guilty and accepting makes her feel trapped. The chair is comfortable in the exact way official rooms use comfort to remind students they are smaller than the desk across from them.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear why she was summoned->Ch7 A New Path 03]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"Is this a warning or a threat?" Pela asks. "A warning," Lysander says. "If it becomes a threat, you will not get a conversation first." Pela believes him. That is the worst part.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Accept the danger->Ch7 A New Path 18]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Tama's spell folds inward. For a second she looks furious enough to keep standing through anything. Then the Saint's unseen pressure passes over her like a hand closing around a candle flame. Tama's eyes roll back. She drops before Pela can reach her. <span class="voice">"There it is,"</span> the Saint murmurs, amused. <span class="voice">"Weakness pretending to be royalty. She wanted a feast and could not bear the first bite."</span> Pela's hands remain at her sides. That should matter. It does not feel like it will.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Call for help before anyone misunderstands->Ch6 The Unseen 42]]</div></div>(set: $tamaRead to true)(set: $tamaFocus to $tamaFocus + 1)(set: $research to $research + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Research") <div class="narrative-box">Pela stops watching the shine and studies the structure. For this reason she has to choose what kind of preparation will keep her from walking into the room already beaten.</div> <div class="choice-list"> <div class="choice-row">[[Practice her own spear skills->Weekend Day One Spear Practice]]</div> <div class="choice-row">[[Visit Odelyn for Spellblade advice->Weekend Day One Odelyn Advice]]</div> <div class="choice-row">[[Ask the Forbidden One for a lesson->Weekend Day One Forbidden Lesson]]</div> </div><div class="narrative-box">Pela had to take her time to master the spear before her first Spellblade class. She had no idea the skill level of the other students. They could be complete amateurs, or they could be masters. For this reason she had to be at her very best.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Practice until the shape answers->Weekend Spear Practice Hours]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">As the weekend hours go by, Pela wants to gain some insight from Odelyn about Spellblade and what is in store for her. Pela thinks about Odelyn and admits that they seem to have a good relationship with each other, but Odelyn has always been an odd individual to her. She understands Pela because of their shared ostracized life, albeit for different reasons.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Think about what draws them together->Weekend Odelyn Close Friend]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela opens her grimoire once again and sees The Forbidden One. The room goes dark and it greets her again. <span class="forbidden-voice">"Pela, you've come for my guidance once again."</span> It finishes its remark while Pela's thoughts are racing. Pela knows she must be respectful, and must ask the demon the right questions.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask for guidance carefully->Weekend Forbidden Respectful Ask]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">The second day comes with old ache in Pela's fingers. The first Spellblade class is close enough now that even resting feels like a decision. She can spend the remaining hours one more way before the weekend becomes something she has to prove in front of everyone.</div> <div class="choice-list"> (if: $weekendDayOneSpear is true or $weekendSpearReady is true or $weapon >= 5)[<div class="choice-row">[[Take the spear to the training grounds->Weekend Day Two Practiced Form]]</div>](else:)[<div class="choice-row choice-row-locked">Take the spear to the training grounds - Pela has not found her spear's shape yet.</div>] <div class="choice-row">[[Visit Gareth for Spellblade advice->Weekend Day Two Gareth Advice]]</div> <div class="choice-row">[[Write to her parents->Weekend Day Two Parents Letter]]</div> </div><div class="narrative-box">Now that Pela understood what her spear truly was, she was determined to make it last longer than a few minutes. To her, her attempts were a complete failure that still only lasted no more than a few minutes. Pela wanted to make it last even longer, but she couldn't figure out how to make it happen.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Admit what kind of lesson she needs->Weekend Practiced Form Application]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela visits Gareth in his dorm room. "Hey, Pela," Gareth greets, his voice cheerful. "What brings you here?"</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask for advice and take the friendly jab->Weekend Gareth Friendly Jab]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela thinks about her family and her childhood before she left for Torrindale. She wonders how her mom and dad are doing. She has not had a back and forth conversation with them for quite a long time at this point.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Remember when stories were kind->Weekend Parents Childhood Stories]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela practiced for hours upon hours but could not seem to get it right. She kept trying to manifest her spear, and could not help but remember how Odelyn's looked. It was a dark black color, and she could feel the power it radiated. She imagined it in her mind nearly perfectly... but that is when she finally realized where she went wrong.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Understand the mistake->Weekend Spear Not Odelyn]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela finally understood. It has to be her own spear. She can't keep modeling herself after Odelyn. She has to be her own person. It can't be Odelyn's spear, but Spark. Pela's spear has to be her own. That's why she was only able to keep it manifested for a few seconds. Because she couldn't imagine her own spear.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Imagine Spark as her own weapon->Weekend Spear Own Shape]]</div></div>(set: $weapon to $weapon + 1)(set: $weekendSpearReady to true)(set: $weekendDayOneSpear to true)(set: $gain to "+1 Weapon, Spear Ready") (display: "Journal Unlock Pela Spear")<div class="narrative-box">Pela focused and made it happen. Her spear was a bright gold and white color, almost like the color of the sun. It was a long spear with a curved tip and a small hook at the end. Through practice, she was now able to make the spear manifest for minutes at a time. The practice left her with a lot of ache, but now at least she was more confident. Not completely confident, but definitely more comfortable now. Pela went to sleep, looking forward to the next day feeling more prepared for her coming Spellblade class.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the second day arrive->Weekend Day Two]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Still, Pela never saw Odelyn in a negative light because she was cursed, but rather as a peer. That's what, admittedly, drew them to each other. Pela doesn't have many friends, but she would consider Odelyn a close friend. As she thinks this, she goes to find her.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Find Odelyn at the training grounds->Weekend Odelyn Training Grounds]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">When Pela finds Odelyn, she is practicing in the training grounds with a dummy. "Hello, Odelyn." "Oh... Hello, Pela," Odelyn replies, her voice curious. "What are you doing here?" "I was wondering if you could tell me more about Spellblade, and what I am in for?" Pela requests, her voice hopeful.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Listen to what Odelyn can safely say->Weekend Odelyn Induction Warning]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I don't want to give you too much information as it's frowned upon for inductees. It's supposed to be an experience everyone gets, but I will tell you that the first day will be grueling. You will be inducted with a fight against someone who definitely is more skilled than you at this point," Odelyn explains, her voice sympathetic. "It will be a test of your skill and willpower. Just know... I believe in you." Odelyn finishes with worry in her voice. "Thank you," Pela responds, her voice grateful. "I will do my best."</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask if anything else can help->Weekend Odelyn Stance Practice]]</div></div>(set: $odelynRoute to $odelynRoute + 1)(set: $weapon to $weapon + 1)(set: $trust to $trust + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Trust, +1 Weapon, +1 Odelyn Route") <div class="narrative-box">Pela looks to the side before leaving. "Anything else that can help me?" "Work on your stance. This one is a close range fighter. He is an offensive fighter and is likely going to go at you and won't take it easy," Odelyn warns, her voice stern. "I will," Pela promises, her voice determined. With that, Pela practices alongside Odelyn for a few hours before calling it a night. She works on her stance and Odelyn corrects her while also honing her own skills.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the second day arrive->Weekend Day Two]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">She knew what she had to do. It was the exact same grief all her teachers accosted her for. She had to learn through application of real life situations rather than theory. Pela knew that the only way she could make her spear last longer was to practice instead of being held up in her room.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Head to the training grounds->Weekend Practiced Form Grounds]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">With her mind set, she headed to the training grounds. There she practiced for a few more hours. Every time the spear flickered, she forced herself to remember that the shape belonged to her. Not Odelyn. Not the Forbidden One. Not the class waiting to measure her. Hers.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Push until the spear stays->Weekend Practiced Form Earned]]</div></div>(set: $practicedForm to true)(set: $gain to "Practiced Form") <div class="narrative-box">Pela was able to keep her spear manifested for over fifteen minutes. However, that toll completely left her without any mana and her body completely aching. She now needed to rest for tomorrow if she planned to be in tip-top shape for her first day of Spellblade.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Spellblade arrive->Two Days Later]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">She remembers the times that they would read to her, and their favorite stories. Stories when the world seemed so kind and it was at a time where she did not have to worry about the horns on her head, the tone of her skin, or the sharpness of her ears. It was a simpler time, when her parents would put her to sleep.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the nostalgia become a letter->Weekend Parents Begin Letter]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">All this nostalgia makes her want to reach out to her parents. She wants to tell them that she is okay, and that she misses them. No matter what happens in the future, she'll get to talk to them now. She gets out paper and a quill and writes a letter to them to clear her mind and heart.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Write what she can bear to say->Weekend Parents Clear Heart]]</div></div>(set: $self to $self + 1)(set: $oath to $oath - 1)(set: $clearMindHeart to true)(set: $gain to "+1 Self, Clear of Mind and Heart") <div class="narrative-box">Pela writes about the events of the past few weeks and how she has been doing in school. She does not write everything. She does not know how to make the Saint, the book, or the shape of the spear sound like anything that would not hurt them from far away. But she writes enough. By the time the last line dries, the noise in her head has somewhere else to live.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Spellblade arrive->Two Days Later]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela starts, "Forbidden One, I need to understand how to use spells and mana more efficiently. You..." She swallows and hates to admit it. "You helped me understand how demons interact with magic better." Pela finishes her sentence with a thought. And you're the only person who will help me, she thought, her mind conflicted.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear what it hears in her->Weekend Forbidden One Of Us]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box"><span class="forbidden-voice">"Of course, Pela,"</span> The Forbidden One replies, clearly hearing both her voice and her thoughts. His voice then becomes ominous and speaks in a low tone. <span class="forbidden-voice">"You are one of us. You may not know it yet, but you are."</span> Pela snaps, "I don't care about all that! Just teach me already..." <span class="forbidden-voice">"Of course,"</span> The Forbidden One replies.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the lesson become stranger->Weekend Forbidden Beyond Fusion]]</div></div>(set: $forbidden to $forbidden + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Forbidden") <div class="narrative-box"><span class="forbidden-voice">"Your professors have already told you about Fusion, but what if I told you that you can fuse more than just spells together?"</span> The Forbidden One asks. "What do you mean?" <span class="forbidden-voice">"Demons can use their emotions to layer their magical abilities as well as spells. You, being a half-demon, can do this as well."</span> "I don't quite understand," Pela admits. <span class="forbidden-voice">"It's simple. You fuse a spell and your emotions. Let me give you an example to make things easier for you to understand."</span></div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Listen to the example->Weekend Forbidden Hatred Spark]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box"><span class="forbidden-voice">"Let's say you want to cast Spark. When you do so, you can also layer on an emotion to the spell, and it will enhance the spell."</span> The Forbidden One lets the dark sit on the word emotion a little too long. <span class="forbidden-voice">"If you cast Spark and are filled with pure hatred, your Spark can become an explosion of pure electric energy, which will incinerate anything it touches."</span> Pela's eyes are wide and her mouth is open. "Wow," she gasps. That is insane, she thought, her mind amazed. That's insane!</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Practice what should probably not be practiced->Weekend Forbidden Shame Practice]]</div></div>(set: $shame to $shame + 1)(set: $nerve to $nerve - 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Shame") <div class="narrative-box">With that, the Forbidden One and Pela take that newfound knowledge and both equally gain from that conversation. They start practicing and honing Pela's abilities. The lesson works. That is the part Pela hates most. The Spark answers faster when she lets something ugly touch it.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the second day arrive->Weekend Day Two]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I know you might not be the best person to ask, but what do you think I should do to prepare for Spellblade tomorrow?" Pela genuinely asks while taking a friendly jab at Gareth for losing so bad to Odelyn. She is laughing on the inside and hopes he will take that in good humor. "I'm not the right person to ask? Ouch," Gareth replies, his voice feigning hurt. "That was just a minor setback," he says in an attempt to recover his pride.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Gareth recover his pride->Weekend Gareth Vayne Warning]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"But, you're right. From what I know of Professor Vayne, she likes to push her students quite a bit." Gareth thinks for a moment, as if deciding how comforting honesty is supposed to be. "So if she thinks you're weak, she will place you against a strong opponent. If she thinks you are strong, she will make you face a very difficult opponent. Either way, she will make you fight someone who is a challenge." Pela winces in pain at that realization.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear the weird compliment->Weekend Gareth Challenge Compliment]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"You will have to show her that you are strong, and capable of facing anyone who she throws your way. Think of it as a compliment in a weird way," Gareth says in an attempt to make Pela feel better. "There really isn't anything else you could let me know?" Pela asks, her tone hopeful. "Well..." Gareth scratches his neck.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Listen for the useful part->Weekend Gareth Impact Advice]]</div></div>(set: $garethRoute to $garethRoute + 1)(set: $research to $research + 1)(set: $trust to $trust + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Research, +1 Trust") <div class="narrative-box">"I've heard he is from Iluus and uses impact magic, so as long as you were paying attention in Professor Belladonna's class it shouldn't be anything you haven't seen before." And the Empire had no trouble discarding what did not fit through.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask about the third stage->Ch9 Third Stage]]</div><div class="choice-row">(link: "Calculate how many teams fail.")[(set: $research to $research + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Research")(goto: "Ch9 Calculate Failing Teams")]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"It's points based on the spells we cast and our performance against our opponent," Lorne explained. "There are only a few slots for the finals. The better you do, the better your chance." "Who are the best mages in Brittanica?" Gareth asked. "Kyrehae, Prince Reglio, Raithgar, and Prince Nalto's team are all from the Academy of Cinn."</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask who Prince Nalto is->Ch9 Prince Nalto]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"Nalto is a member of the royal family, but not a direct descendant of the Empire," Lorne said. "Besides, his team will not win." "How do you know that?" Pela challenged. "Because I don't believe the Emperor would sponsor such a weak team," Lorne said, voice suddenly pained. "Nalto was exiled for who he chose to associate himself with."</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">(link: "Hear the pain in Lorne's answer.")[(set: $trust to $trust + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Trust")(goto: "Ch9 Hear Lorne Pain")]</div><div class="choice-row">(link: "Remember Nalto's name.")[(set: $research to $research + 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Research")(goto: "Ch9 Remember Nalto Name")]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I can't believe someone from the royal family could be exiled," Odelyn mused. "He was. Now let's get to the second stage," Lorne ordered. "Alright, Lorne," Pela agreed. "Lead the way." The Salt Colosseum waited ahead, white and enormous, like the Empire had carved judgment into stone.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[End Chapter 9 for now->Chapter Nine End]]</div>(if: $self >= 4)[<div class="choice-row choice-row-unclaimed">(link: "Follow the team without giving the Empire her fear (DC Self: 4)")[(set: $self to $self + 1)(set: $oath to $oath - 1)(set: $gain to "+1 Self")(goto: "Ch9 Unclaimed Toward Colosseum")]</div>]</div><div class="narrative-box">Chapters 8 and 9 end here for now. The Mage-Card exam has begun. The first stage has already tested whether they can enter the capital. The second waits inside the Salt Colosseum.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Return to Main Menu->Main Menu]]</div><div class="choice-row">[[Jump to a test moment->Jump to Moment]]</div></div>(display: "Tester Jump Core Stats")(display: "Tester Jump Post Lorne State")(set: $learnedBecomeLightning to true)(set: $odelynLostBattleWon to true)(set: $tamaOutcome to "battle")(set: $chapterEightStarted to true) <div class="tester-jump-box"> <div class="menu-page-title">Tester Jump: Before Ardenfelt Road Ambush</div> <p>Pela has been prepared for Chapter 8 and 9 testing. Core visible stats are set to 20, Fusion is set to 6, and post-Lorne systems remain unlocked.</p> <p>This jump goes directly to the Ardenfelt POV ambush and battle. It does not touch checkpoint saves.</p> </div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Start Ardenfelt's road ambush->Ardenfelt POV Roadblock]]</div><div class="choice-row">[[Start Chapter 8 from the dream->Chapter Eight Hook]]</div><div class="choice-row">[[Choose another moment->Jump to Moment]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela rejects the word before it can become true simply because someone else said it. "Monster is lazy," she says. "People use it when they are too afraid to explain what they mean." The man in the fog does not move. The roses do.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Make him answer anyway->Ch8 Dream Darkness]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela lets the word monster touch her. Not because she believes it. Because sometimes pain is easier to study after it stops pretending to be new. The roses lean closer. Their sweetness becomes almost physical, and Pela hates that a beautiful thing can feel so cruel.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask what the wound means->Ch8 Dream Darkness]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela hears the contradiction first. Cannot be saved. Can be redeemed. The words fit together too neatly, like someone built a cage and called it guidance. She does not know who the voice belongs to, but she knows when someone is trying to make surrender sound holy.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Follow the lie to the roses->Ch8 Rose Destiny]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box unclaimed-box"><span class="unclaimed-mark"></span>Pela stands straighter inside the dream. "I am not a curse to be redeemed," she says. The sentence feels dangerous. Not loud. Not heroic. Just hers. For a moment, the dark does not know where to put its hands.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-unclaimed">[[Keep the sentence even when the dream pushes back->Ch8 Rose Destiny]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box eldritch-box"><span class="eldritch-mark"></span>The roses smell sweet. Then they smell hungry. Pela does not step back. Something in her oath opens one eye and approves of that restraint. The beautiful scent presses against her throat like teeth deciding whether to become a smile.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-eldritch">[[Let the dream pretend it is still only a warning->Ch8 Rose Destiny]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela memorizes the scent like a spell component. Sweetness first. Then rot underneath it. Then something old enough to make the difference feel meaningless. If the roses bloom again, she wants to know before the dream has time to explain itself.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Wake with the scent still in her mouth->Ch8 Wake Late]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Anger reaches Pela before fear can organize itself. Good. Fear makes her freeze. Anger makes her move. She grabs the edge of the dream with both hands and tears herself awake before the roses can open all the way.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Come back to the room hard enough to breathe->Ch8 Wake Late]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela dresses so quickly the buttons feel like enemies. Her hair refuses to behave. Her papers slide off the desk. One shoe hides under the bed like it has decided the Mage-Card exam is none of its business. "Not today," Pela mutters, and runs.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Arrive before lateness becomes another accusation->Ch8 Dean Office]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela should leave immediately. Instead, she grabs a pen and writes one word. Roses. The ink looks too dark on the page. She stares at it for half a second too long, then curses herself for wasting time and runs anyway.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Take the note and the lateness with her->Ch8 Dean Office]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Dean Sainstroy smiles with practiced warmth. Pela watches his eyes instead. They are kind, or shaped like kindness, which is not always the same thing. He looks at her like a student. He also looks at her like a problem that has arrived before the paperwork is ready.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Wait for the paper hidden under the smile->Ch8 Written Score]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela accepts the praise carefully. She wants it to feel good. It does, a little. Then she remembers that praise from the Academy often comes with a hook in it, and she keeps her hands where she can see them.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the compliment finish turning->Ch8 Grades Slip]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela has learned not to trust congratulations that arrive alone. They usually bring relatives. Expectation. Correction. Threat. She waits, and the Dean's voice proves her right by becoming softer before it becomes worse.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear what the praise was protecting->Ch8 Grades Slip]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"Professor Ardenfelt is difficult," Pela admits. The Dean's expression sharpens. "But difficult is not the same thing as wrong," she adds quickly. "He has helped me more than most professors have." She hates how true that is. She hates more that defending him feels like defending the bruise because it taught her where the table was.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Sainstroy move to the real reason->Ch8 Mage Card Law]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela lists what she has. Spark. A spear that sometimes obeys. A shield she learned by nearly being thrown through a classroom wall. Fusion, if the spells do not decide to kill her for arrogance. It is not enough. It is also more than she had when the semester began.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the exam become real anyway->Ch8 Execution Memory]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"I will not fail," Pela says. The words come out too fast. Sainstroy studies her for a moment. He does not comfort her. Maybe that is his version of respect. "Then make sure that is not merely optimism."</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Accept that optimism is not enough->Ch8 Prepare Tomorrow]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"When do we leave?" It is the most useful question Pela can find, which is why she asks it before terror can drag her into something dramatic. Sainstroy nods once. No one says she has permission. The closing door gives her the answer anyway.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear the answer she cannot delay->Ch8 Prepare Tomorrow]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela thinks of her parents and says nothing. If she fails, they will not just lose her. They will lose the memory of losing her. The cruelty of that feels too large to fit in her chest, so it folds itself smaller and becomes shame instead.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Carry the silence into tomorrow->Ch8 Prepare Tomorrow]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box unclaimed-box"><span class="unclaimed-mark"></span>Pela decides one thing before leaving the office. She will not pass as Ardenfelt's correction. She will not pass as the Saint's appetite. She will not pass as the Forbidden One's crony. If she survives, she will survive as Pela Dianthus, and she does not know whether that is bravery or stubbornness.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-unclaimed">[[Take that decision into dawn->Ch8 Cart Dawn]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Forgotten. The word follows Pela out of the office and down the hall. She does not know if the Academy means erased from record, memory, history, or all of it. She only knows that she suddenly wants to leave a mark so deep no spell can clean it out.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Meet the cart with the word still following->Ch8 Cart Dawn]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela stands closer to Odelyn. Not close enough for anyone to comment. Close enough that Odelyn notices. Odelyn's eyes flick toward her, then away. She does not smile, but her shoulder eases by the smallest amount, and Pela understands that as clearly as any sentence.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the cart gather all of them together->Ch8 Cart Ardenfelt]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela gets in the cart before Ardenfelt can make hesitation educational. Gareth follows quickly. Lorne tries to make entering a cart look noble and fails because it is still a cart. Odelyn says nothing, but her silence has the shape of someone counting enemies.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask the question once everyone is trapped together->Ch8 Excommunication Explained]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela notices the way Lorne says transfer. Not like a door. Like a punishment that learned how to wear school colors. For one uncomfortable moment, Lorne looks less like a prince and more like a boy who had already lost somewhere else before he came here.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the silence expose what pride hides->Ch8 Lorne Transfer Silence]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela lets the wound stay unnamed. It surprises her that she can do that. Lorne has earned plenty of cruelty from her. Still, some things feel too private to touch even when the person bleeding from them deserves nothing.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Sit with the silence until the road stops->Ch8 Road Stop]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela files the detail away. Iluus. Transfer. Excommunication. Lorne's arrogance is not smaller because she understands part of it. If anything, it becomes worse. It means he knows exactly how sharp the system is and still throws other people toward the edge.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Keep the detail until it matters->Ch8 Road Stop]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela watches the trees instead of Ardenfelt. The road is too quiet. Leaves move without wind. Shadows sit too heavily between trunks. Even before Ardenfelt steps out of the cart, Pela understands that something has been waiting for them with patience.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear Ardenfelt make the danger simple->Ch8 Ardenfelt Silences Odelyn]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Bubble of Silence. Pela memorizes the shape by watching Odelyn fail to speak. It is an ugly thing to learn from a friend's frustration, but magic does not become less useful because the lesson is rude.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Watch Ardenfelt stay behind with the spell still fresh->Ch8 Ardenfelt Road Alone]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box ardenfelt-box"><span class="ardenfelt-title">Ardenfelt POV</span> Ardenfelt looks at the staff before he looks at the men. People lie. Relics are usually more honest about the damage they were built to do. The ruby at the top glows faintly, and Ardenfelt's annoyance becomes interest by the smallest possible measurement.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Name what Athea left behind->Ardenfelt POV Staff Adam]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box ardenfelt-box"><span class="ardenfelt-title">Ardenfelt POV</span> Ardenfelt gives them the courtesy of his contempt. "You did not ambush my students," he says. "You scheduled your own humiliation poorly." The second cultist stiffens. Good. At least one of them understands tone.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Lucian mistake contempt for conversation->Ardenfelt POV Threats]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box ardenfelt-box">Ardenfelt names the relic's danger in silence. Soul-binding. Amplification. Old Athean pride polished until it can pass for sacred history. He does not say any of this aloud. Teaching an enemy why they are doomed is only satisfying after they have run out of ways to benefit from the explanation.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Lucian introduce the mistake formally->Ardenfelt POV Threats]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela shares the awe with Gareth because he is the only one not trying to own the view. "It is beautiful," she says. Gareth nods. "It makes me feel like I should stand up straighter." Pela almost laughs. Then she realizes she is doing it too.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Lorne ruin the moment on schedule->Ch9 Lorne Legacy]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela keeps watching the city instead of Lorne. Walls. Wards. Flowers. Silver gates. Old money pretending to be architecture. The capital is beautiful in the way a blade can be beautiful when it is clean and pointed at someone else.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear Lorne make beauty about himself->Ch9 Lorne Legacy]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box jerk-box"><span class="nerve-mark"></span>"You are brave for someone who loses loudly," Pela says. Lorne's mouth opens. For once, no royal speech comes out immediately. It is a small victory, but it is hers, and the look on his face is worth whatever extreme reaction he will have.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-jerk">[[Let Odelyn decide that was not enough->Ch9 Odelyn Slap]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela lets monster pass through her without answering. It does not pass cleanly. The word leaves hooks. Still, the exam is bigger than Lorne's cruelty, and Pela hates that survival sometimes asks her to be quiet around people who deserve worse.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Odelyn answer what Pela swallowed->Ch9 Odelyn Slap]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela sees it then. Odelyn is not only defending her, she defending more than Pela. She is defending the idea that cursed does not mean disposable... the right to be cursed and still matter. That the title 'monster' does not become truth just because a prince says it in public. Pela does not know how to thank someone for fighting a word she has been carrying for years.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear Odelyn make her title dangerous->Ch9 Odelyn Royal Threat]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box romance-box"><span class="romance-heart"></span>Pela looks at Odelyn like the defense mattered. Because it did. Odelyn notices. Her anger does not soften, not really, but it turns enough for Pela to see the worry underneath. For one second, all the noise of the gate becomes quieter than the space between them.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-romance">[[Follow before the moment becomes too visible->Ch9 Gate Guard]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"Thank you," Pela says properly. The guard blinks as if politeness was not one of the spells he expected from Torrindale students. "Good luck," he replies. It sounds official. It also sounds like an apology he is not allowed to make.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Notice what he called the second stage->Ch9 Second Stage]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela enjoys the expression on Lorne's face. She should not. She absolutely does. There is something deeply satisfying about watching a prince discover that invisible things still count when they are stronger than his confidence.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Explain the barrier before he invents another excuse->Ch9 Pela Sees Barrier]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela maps the barrier in her mind. It is not a wall. Not exactly. It is an Impact Shield made enormous, spread across the gate like transparent cloth, layered with recognition magic and pressure points that punish arrogance. No wonder Lorne hit it face first.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Watch arrogance test the structure again->Ch9 Mock Lorne]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Odelyn's shadow magic does not bounce off the barrier the same way Lorne's impact magic did. It drags at the ward. The barrier resists, then thins, like it is deciding whether a curse counts as a student or an infection. Pela hates the question before she fully understands it.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask if Odelyn is alright with more than her pride->Ch9 Odelyn Mana Decay]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela admires Odelyn without making it obvious. Mana Decay is terrifying up close. Not flashy. Not pretty. Just the quiet certainty of taking a thing apart by touching it. Odelyn steps through the opening she made like she was always supposed to be there.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Gareth try to make the exam make sense->Ch9 Gareth Barrier Theory]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"That was almost elegant," Pela tells Gareth. "Almost?" "Do not get greedy." Gareth smiles despite the barrier, and for a second the exam feels less like an execution machine and more like something they might survive by being themselves.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Watch Lorne reject elegance for force->Ch9 Lorne Overwhelming Impact]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela steps back before pride becomes collateral. Lorne does not. That is the difference between knowing danger and believing danger should ask permission first. The knight reaches for him, and the air changes shape around the motion.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Watch the prince introduce himself with violence->Ch9 Raithgar Grabs Lorne]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela remembers both names before she understands why they matter. Raithgar. Kyrehae. The names feel heavy in the air, not because they are royal, but because everyone around them makes space for the violence attached to them.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Watch Kyrehae make violence obey etiquette->Ch9 Kyrehae Intervenes]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Kyrehae's slap is healing and insult together. Mana moves through the strike with cruel precision. Enough to wake Lorne. Enough to hurt. Not enough to apologize. Pela studies it because Brittanica keeps teaching her that kindness is not the only reason people put bodies back together.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Thank her because survival still counts->Ch9 Kyrehae Dismisses]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela keeps the insult instead of the fear. You and your friends. Stronger. Kyrehae said it like weakness was a personal inconvenience the world had no obligation to tolerate. Pela hates her immediately. She also understands the warning.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let Lorne name the people they have to survive->Ch9 Academy Cinn Names]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Lorne sounds defeated before he says the third name. That is what frightens Pela. Lorne has been angry, embarrassed, cruel, arrogant, and stupid. This is different. This is what he sounds like when he believes the outcome has already happened.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask about the name that made him smaller->Ch9 Reglio Rumor]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">"What kind of person scares you?" Pela asks. Lorne glares. The answer sits behind his teeth and refuses to come out with dignity. "The kind you do not understand until you are already beneath them," he says finally, and Pela realizes he is not trying to sound dramatic.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Help him up with the answer still between them->Ch9 Lorne Crawl]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela lets Odelyn scare him for one second. One. That is all. Lorne has thrown the word monster at Pela like a stone so many times that watching fear return to his own face feels almost fair. Then almost becomes too close to enough, and Pela moves.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Stop Odelyn before fear becomes damage they cannot undo->Ch9 Odelyn Curse]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela wonders why Odelyn is this hard on him. It is not only anger. There is history in it, or recognition, or some ugly mixture of both. Odelyn looks at Lorne like he is not the first royal boy to learn cruelty as a language and mistake it for inheritance.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Walk while the question follows behind them->Ch9 Salt Colosseum Approach]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela studies the guards watching from too far away. They see the students. They see the empty path. They do not approach. That is when the street stops feeling deserted and starts feeling prepared.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Notice what the silence is making room for->Ch9 Desolate Path]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela reaches for Spark before knowing why. The magic answers quickly, almost too quickly, a warmth under her skin that wants to become light. She does not summon the spear. Not yet. But her hand remembers the shape.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Hear what the street is hiding->Ch9 Humming Begins]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela listens to the rhythm of the hum. It is not music. It is magic moving with enough control to pass for silence until it chooses otherwise. The sound crawls over her skin, and every instinct in her body asks why the city is letting it approach.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[See the person the hum belongs to->Ch9 Reglio Appears]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela keeps breathing through the pressure. In. Out. Again. Reglio passes without looking at her, and somehow that is worse than being noticed. It makes her feel like scenery in her own fear.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Feel his presence arrive late and still overwhelm them->Ch9 Reglio Presence]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela admits it to herself. Reglio's magic is beautiful. It is also terrifying. Those two things do not cancel each other out. If anything, the beauty makes the terror worse, because it means power can wear elegance and still crush everything beneath it.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Listen to everyone fail to name him properly->Ch9 Angel And Demon]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box eldritch-box"><span class="eldritch-mark"></span>The Saint admires the royal storm. Not with fear. With appetite. Pela feels the oath shift under her skin like something sitting up to watch the procession. Reglio does not look at her, but the hunger inside her smiles anyway.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-eldritch">[[Swallow the hunger before anyone sees it->Ch9 Angel And Demon]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box romance-box"><span class="romance-heart"></span>Pela shares the fear with Gareth without joking. "I do not like how small he makes the road feel," she says quietly. Gareth looks at her, then at Reglio's back. "Me neither." It does not comfort her. It steadies her, which is rarer.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-romance">[[Ask the question neither of them wants answered->Ch9 Odelyn Vows]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela stands with Odelyn against the word cursed. Not loudly. Lorne would only turn it into a fight. But she moves closer, the same way she did at the cart, and Odelyn notices again. This time her eyes soften for less than a heartbeat before pride covers it.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the exam swallow the argument for now->Ch9 Tournament Rules]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela calculates how many teams fail. Too many. The numbers are not comforting. They never are. They turn fear into shape, but shape is not mercy. The Empire built the exam like a funnel and called it opportunity.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Ask what waits after the funnel narrows->Ch9 Third Stage]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela hears the pain in Lorne's answer. She does not forgive him. The two things are unrelated. But for one second, she understands that he is not only repeating the Empire's cruelty because he enjoys it. He is repeating it because it already taught him where to bleed.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Let the pain point them toward the Colosseum->Ch9 Lead Way]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box">Pela remembers Nalto's name. Exiled royal. Sponsored team. Someone the Emperor would rather keep at the edge of the family than outside the game entirely. Names matter in Brittanica. Sometimes they are weapons. Sometimes they are chains.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row">[[Keep the name for when it becomes a problem->Ch9 Lead Way]]</div></div><div class="narrative-box unclaimed-box"><span class="unclaimed-mark"></span>Pela follows the team without giving the Empire her fear. The fear is still there. She is not stupid. But it does not get to lead. Not this time. She lets her own feet choose the direction, and for once the oath inside her has nothing useful to say.</div> <div class="choice-list"><div class="choice-row choice-row-unclaimed">[[End Chapter 9 for now->Chapter Nine End]]</div></div><div class="journal-window"> <div class="journal-head"><div class="journal-title">Pela's Journal</div><div class="journal-subtitle">Pages appear when Pela has enough $journalPage is "Torrindale" and $journalTorrindale is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Torrindale University</div><div class="journal-page-body">I thought getting accepted would feel like proof that I belong, but it mostly feels like being invited into a room where everyone has already decided what I am.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Home" and $journalHome is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Home</div><div class="journal-page-body">Before Torrindale, home was warm enough that I could forget people were afraid of people like me elsewhere. I wonder if my parents knew about the world outside Orgoshk and its people. People in the central Brittanican cities are far more judgemental.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Spark" and $journalSpark is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Spark Magic</div><div class="journal-page-body">Spark does not feel like fire. It does not feel like lightning either. The formula for understanding it in class is much more complex than a lot of the other magical elements. I wonder why it comes to me so easily.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Saint" and $journalSaint is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">The Saint of the Feast</div><div class="journal-page-body">The Saint does not speak like a voice in my head. It feels like gnawing hunger that keeps trying to influence my thoughts and actions. I need to figure out how to deal with it before it becomes too much...</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Forbidden" and $journalForbidden is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">The Forbidden One</div><div class="journal-page-body">The Forbidden One teaches too well, and that is the worst part because a lie would be easier to hate than a truth that helps me. I hope I do not rely on that thing too much in the future.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Odelyn" and $journalOdelyn is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Odelyn</div><div class="journal-page-body">Odelyn is cursed. People say that like it explains her, but it is just one of those labels that Brittanicans put on people. It does not explain her at all. If anything, it explains everyone who looks at her and only sees that label.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "ArdenfeltOne" and $journalArdenfeltOne is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Professor Ardenfelt I</div><div class="journal-page-body">I cannot tell if Ardenfelt wants to help me or not. I can't get a read on him and I hate him more than any other faculty member here. Maybe that will change now that he sees I can cast Spark magic.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Gareth" and $journalGareth is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Gareth</div><div class="journal-page-body">Gareth jokes when the room gets sharp. I can't get a good read on him, however I think he hides something behind the humor he openly displays.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Lorne" and $journalLorne is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Lorne</div><div class="journal-page-body">Lorne speaks like cruelty is his inheritance. I do not know if he believes everything he says, or if he is afraid of what would happen if he stopped.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "NegativeImpact" and $journalNegativeImpact is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Negative Impact Magic</div><div class="journal-page-body">Negative Impact does not push. It pulls. That sounds simple until magic drags your body through the air and makes the floor feel nonexistent.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "ImpactShield" and $journalImpactShield is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Impact Shield</div><div class="journal-page-body">I blocked Belladonna's spell. I still do not fully understand how to nullify it, but I am confident that harsh lesson can help me in a practical way... even though he is probably more rude than Ardenfelt.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "PelaSpear" and $journalPelaSpear is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Pela's Spear</div><div class="journal-page-body">I kept trying to make the spear look like someone else's. It did not hold until I stopped borrowing a shape of the people I see around me and let it become mine. If I think honestly, maybe that's why other magics do not work well for me. Spark found me, just like this spear.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "SpellbladeCombat" and $journalSpellbladeCombat is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Spellblade Combat</div><div class="journal-page-body">Fighting Lorne taught me that combat is not just power. It is rhythm. Fear. Pride. Execution. It is the second before someone decides what they truly are and what they stand for.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Tama" and $journalTama is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Tama</div><div class="journal-page-body">Tama acts like the world is supposed to make room for her. Maybe that is what royalty is and I think that is one of the great shames of Brittanica... confidence sharpened until everyone else mistakes it for law.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "BecomeLightning" and $journalBecomeLightning is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Become Lightning</div><div class="journal-page-body">I did not stop being afraid. Fear moved, and for once, I moved faster.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "MageCard" and $journalMageCard is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Mage-Card Exam</div><div class="journal-page-body">The Mage-Card Exam is not a test. It is execution with paperwork, and everyone keeps saying it like that makes it normal. Truth be told, I hope we all make it out of this exam in one piece.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Excommunication" and $journalExcommunication is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Excommunication</div><div class="journal-page-body">Excommunication means they can take your magic and call it discipline. I used to think failing meant being sent home. In Brittanican schools, failing means being erased. Maybe that's why Belladonna and Ardenfelt were so hard on me. I did not know it at the time, but my time was ticking.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "ArdenfeltTwo" and $journalArdenfeltTwo is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Professor Ardenfelt II</div><div class="journal-page-body">Ardenfelt stayed behind, and the road behind us felt safer than the road ahead. That should not be possible. I think that is the point of him. I have complete confidence in him.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Reglio" and $journalReglio is true)[<article class="journal-page-card"><div class="journal-page-content"><div><div class="journal-page-title">Reglio</div><div class="journal-page-body">Reglio passed us without looking. I have never felt so clearly that someone could destroy me without needing to hate me first.</div></div><div class="journal-sketch">Sketch space</div></div></article><div class="journal-page-nav"><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Back")</div><div class="journal-page-turn">(display: "Journal Nav Forward")</div></div>] (if: $journalPage is "Torrindale" and $journalTorrindale is
